significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) ordering that an LLM "first retrieves the affirmative fact using the same mid-layer machinery" and only later performs a "shallow, and error-prone" negation override, together with the form-(ii) claim that failed suppression causes negation errors; this fixes where two computations occur and predicts affirmative-answer dominance before late negation integration. It would establish both a phenomenon—polarity-dependent failure after successful retrieval—and a mechanism, sharpening the behavioral negation failures documented by Kassner and Schütze (ACL 2020) and connecting them to the enrichment-then-extraction account of factual recall in Geva et al. (EMNLP 2023). Verified false would informatively rule out this serial retrieve-then-override explanation, although it would not by itself distinguish among all alternatives such as early polarity-sensitive retrieval and general instruction failure; true and false are nevertheless determinate states. Topic substitution would leave only a generic question about query-dependent knowledge retrieval, which would not earn this score; the specific temporal ordering and causal failure localization are materially stronger than the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: an internal "classifier ... to predict, before the answer, whether a negated query will suffer an override failure" and a training-free "negation-completion" intervention that suppresses the retrieved affirmative direction. The classifier is ex ante and leaves an action window before generation, while the intervention is a deployment-time corrective knob rather than merely a post-hoc explanation. After model-specific re-extraction, the substantive ordering still predicts mid-layer affirmative decodability followed by late negation integration, so more than a search procedure transfers, although the direction and exact integration layer are not claimed invariant; the hypothesis speaks broadly of "an LLM," with likely uptake by interpretability researchers and model auditors or deployers rather than outside-AI users. Under topic substitution these concrete predictor, intervention, and transferable ordering disappear, so the reach score is attributable to the claim rather than to the general importance of knowledge retrieval.
